name: Artificer
summary: Artificers use tools, magic, inventions, infusions, and magic items to produce flexible magical effects. The class is Intelligence-based, uses prepared spellcasting, gains cantrips, creates infused items, and becomes increasingly effective with magic items.
build_notes: The class is centered on Intelligence, prepared spellcasting, tools, infusions, and magic item use.
The class has light armor, medium armor, shields, Constitution saving throws, and Intelligence saving throws.
Subclass choice changes combat role significantly, so base class tagging avoids overcommitting to melee, ranged, tank, or healer.

name: Alchemist
summary: Alchemists use reagents and elixirs to heal, enhance allies, transform creatures, and deal acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage. Their features emphasize experimental elixirs, restorative magic, and chemical resilience.
mechanical_tags: bonus healing or damage through alchemist's supplies
build_notes: Healing and alchemy are the defining traits because Experimental Elixir, Alchemical Savant, Restorative Reagents, and Chemical Mastery all directly support them.
Flight and increased speed are included at low weight because they appear as possible elixir effects rather than always-on subclass identity.
Damage type traits are supported by Alchemical Savant and the subclass spell list, but healing and support are more central.

name: Armorer
summary: Armorers turn armor into Arcane Armor, using it as a magical conduit, weapon platform, and defensive shell. The subclass supports a Guardian model for front-line defense and an Infiltrator model for ranged lightning attacks, movement, and stealth.
build_notes: Heavy armor and Arcane Armor are defining mechanics.
Tank and defender are strongly supported by Guardian model features, especially Thunder Gauntlets and Defensive Field.
Ranged, stealth, and increased speed are included because of the Infiltrator model, but weighted below the armor identity.

name: Artillerist
summary: Artillerists create magical cannons that project fire, force, protection, and battlefield pressure. Their features emphasize destructive spell damage, bonus-action cannon activation, temporary hit point support, and fortified defensive positions.
build_notes: Blaster is the defining role because the subclass description and features focus on energy, projectiles, explosions, cannon damage, and destructive spells.
Support and defender are secondary because Protector and Fortified Position provide temporary hit points and cover.
Climbing is low-weight because it applies only if the cannon has legs and moves or climbs.

name: Battle Smith
summary: Battle Smiths combine martial weapon combat, magical healing, and a steel defender companion. Their features emphasize Intelligence-based weapon attacks, protection, repair, force damage, healing, and a construct companion that acts in combat.
build_notes: The steel defender is the defining subclass mechanic and supports companion, construct, defender, and protect allies tags.
Battle Ready and Extra Attack support weapon-combat tagging.
Arcane Jolt supports both force damage and healing, but neither fully replaces the companion as the subclass identity.

name: Barbarian
summary: Barbarians are rage-fueled martial combatants whose class features emphasize Strength-based melee attacks, resilience, speed, instinct, and survival under heavy punishment. Their core mechanics include Rage, Unarmored Defense, Reckless Attack, Extra Attack, Fast Movement, Brutal Critical, Relentless Rage, and Strength and Constitution scaling.
mechanical_tags: resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing while raging
build_notes: The class is primarily martial, Strength-based, durable, and melee-oriented.
Rage is the defining mechanic and supports offense, resistance, and several later class features.
The base class should not be tagged as spellcasting because Rage explicitly prevents spellcasting and concentration while raging.

name: Path of the Ancestral Guardian
summary: Ancestral Guardian barbarians call on guardian spirits while raging to hinder enemies, protect allies, reduce damage, consult spirits, and retaliate with force damage. The subclass is centered on defense, protection, and ancestral spirit magic.
mechanical_tags: Augury or Clairvoyance without spell slot
build_notes: The subclass is primarily defensive because its first two major combat features hinder enemies and reduce ally damage.
Force is included because Vengeful Ancestors explicitly deals force damage.
Divination and spellcasting are low-weight because Consult the Spirits grants limited spell use rather than normal spellcasting.

name: Path of the Battlerager
summary: Battleragers specialize in spiked armor, close-range melee attacks, grappling damage, temporary hit points, bonus-action dashing, and automatic retaliation damage. The subclass is a rage-based melee bruiser built around armored body attacks.
mechanical_tags: temporary hit points from Reckless Attack

other: Restriction: Dwarves Only, unless lifted by the DM

build_notes: The subclass is centered on wearing spiked armor while raging.
Grappling is meaningful because Battlerager Armor deals piercing damage after a successful grapple check.
Mobility is secondary and comes from Battlerager Charge.

name: Path of the Beast
summary: Path of the Beast barbarians physically transform during rage, manifesting natural weapons such as bite, claws, or tail. Later features add swimming, climbing, enhanced jumping, psychic fury, temporary hit points, and ally damage bonuses.
build_notes: Natural weapons and transformation are the defining subclass identity.
Swimming and climbing are meaningful but optional choices from Bestial Soul.
Support is secondary because Call the Hunt buffs allies but arrives at 14th level.

name: Path of the Berserker
summary: Berserker barbarians embrace violent frenzy, gaining bonus-action melee attacks while raging, immunity to charm and fear while raging, a fear-based presence, and reaction melee attacks when damaged. The subclass emphasizes relentless offense at personal cost.
mechanical_tags: charm and frighten suspension while raging
build_notes: Bonus-action attacks are the defining mechanic because Frenzy directly adds a melee weapon attack each turn while raging.
Exhaustion is included because Frenzy explicitly imposes one level of exhaustion when rage ends.
Fear and Intimidation are meaningful secondary mechanics from Intimidating Presence.

name: Path of the Giant
summary: Path of the Giant barbarians draw on giant and elemental power, growing in size, increasing reach, empowering thrown weapons, infusing weapons with elemental damage, and hurling creatures around the battlefield. The subclass centers on giant stature, thrown weapon combat, elemental weapon damage, and forced movement.
build_notes: Thrown weapons are defining because both Giant's Havoc and Elemental Cleaver directly improve thrown weapon use.
Forced movement is defining because Mighty Impel allows the barbarian to hurl allies and enemies.
Spellcasting and cantrips are low-weight because Giant's Power grants only one cantrip.

name: Path of the Storm Herald
summary: Storm Herald barbarians transform rage into a magical storm aura tied to desert, sea, or tundra. Their features provide fire or lightning damage, temporary hit points, cold, fire, or lightning resistance, swimming, ally protection, reactions, prone effects, and speed reduction.
build_notes: Aura is the defining mechanic because Storm Aura drives the subclass's main recurring effects.
Fire, lightning, and cold are all supported by environment choices.
Controller is secondary because prone and speed reduction are late subclass effects tied to specific environments.

name: Path of the Totem Warrior
summary: Totem Warrior barbarians bond with animal spirits that grant ritual magic and rage-based supernatural benefits. The subclass can emphasize durability, mobility, ally offense, exploration, skill utility, flight bursts, prone effects, and nature-based spirit guidance.
build_notes: This subclass is broad because the page presents multiple totem choices with distinct mechanics.
Beast, spirit, nature, and ritual casting are central across the subclass text.
Flight is included at moderate weight because it is available through one Totemic Attunement choice rather than the whole subclass baseline.

name: Path of Wild Magic
summary: Wild Magic barbarians are suffused with supernatural magic that erupts during rage. Their features detect spells and magic items, trigger randomized magical effects, teleport, deal necrotic, force, or radiant damage, create difficult terrain, protect allies, and bolster attacks, ability checks, or spell slots.
build_notes: Wild magic is the defining identity because Wild Surge is the central recurring subclass mechanic.
Teleportation, damage types, difficult terrain, and blinded are weighted moderately because they are individual results on the Wild Magic table.
Support and buffing are meaningful because Bolstering Magic directly helps the barbarian or a companion.

name: Path of the Zealot
summary: Zealot barbarians channel divine fury into weapon attacks, gaining necrotic or radiant damage, easier restoration to life, saving throw rerolls, ally inspiration, and the ability to keep fighting at 0 hit points while raging. The subclass is a divine warrior focused on offense, resilience, and battle zeal.
mechanical_tags: necrotic or radiant extra weapon damage
ally advantage on attacks and saving throws
build_notes: Divine and striker traits are central because Divine Fury adds recurring damage while raging.
Death prevention is defining at high level because Rage Beyond Death allows the character to continue acting at 0 hit points while raging.
Support is secondary because Zealous Presence helps allies but is limited to once per long rest.

name: Bard
summary: Bards use music, speech, performance, and Charisma-based spellcasting to inspire allies, demoralize foes, manipulate minds, create illusions, and heal wounds. Their core class identity combines full spellcasting, Bardic Inspiration, broad skills, Expertise, Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest, Countercharm, and Magical Secrets.
build_notes: The class is primarily a Charisma-based full caster, support character, face, and skill-focused utility class.
Bardic Inspiration is a defining class resource used to improve ally rolls and later recovered on a short or long rest.
Magical Secrets supports broad utility and flexible spell access, but the base class should not be over-tagged with every possible spell role.

name: College of Creation
summary: College of Creation bards draw on the Song of Creation to enhance Bardic Inspiration, create temporary nonmagical objects, and animate items into dancing constructs. The subclass emphasizes creation, support, temporary hit points, thunder damage, and a commanded animated companion-like object.
mechanical_tags: temporary hit points from saving throw mote
thunder damage from attack roll mote
build_notes: The subclass is primarily a Bardic Inspiration enhancer and magical creator.
Companion feature is included because Animating Performance creates a friendly Dancing Item that acts in combat and can be commanded.
Thunder is secondary because it appears as one Mote of Potential effect rather than the entire subclass identity.

name: College of Eloquence
summary: College of Eloquence bards master persuasion, deception, and magically unsettling speech. Their features improve social checks, weaken enemy saving throws, preserve Bardic Inspiration on failed rolls, enable universal communication, and spread inspiration to additional allies.
mechanical_tags: minimum d20 result for Persuasion and Deception
build_notes: The subclass is strongly centered on Charisma-based social checks and Bardic Inspiration.
Debuffing is central because Unsettling Words directly subtracts from a target's next saving throw.
Language utility is meaningful because Universal Speech lets chosen creatures magically understand the bard.

name: College of Glamour
summary: College of Glamour bards use fey magic, beauty, and performance to charm creatures, grant allies temporary hit points and movement, command creatures, and discourage enemies from attacking them. The subclass emphasizes fey enchantment, social control, mobility support, and defensive majesty.
mechanical_tags: charmed creatures automatically fail Command save
build_notes: Fey, charm, enchantment, and social manipulation are defining because every subclass feature is framed through fey magic, captivating performance, or commanding presence.
Mobility and support are central at early levels through Mantle of Inspiration.
Defensive traits are secondary because Unbreakable Majesty protects the bard by disrupting attacks rather than improving armor directly.

name: College of Lore
summary: College of Lore bards collect knowledge, expose falsehoods, and use wit to reduce enemy competence. Their features emphasize additional skill proficiencies, Cutting Words, extra Magical Secrets, and Bardic Inspiration applied to their own ability checks.
mechanical_tags: Bardic Inspiration penalty to attack roll, ability check, or damage roll
Bardic Inspiration added to own ability check
build_notes: Skill expert and scholar are defining because the subclass gains three skills and is described around broad knowledge.
Debuffing is central because Cutting Words subtracts Bardic Inspiration from enemy rolls.
Utility caster is meaningful because Additional Magical Secrets expands spell access earlier than the base class.

name: College of Spirits
summary: College of Spirits bards channel spirits through occult focuses and supernatural tales. Their features grant Guidance, improve damage or healing through a Spiritual Focus, produce randomized tale effects, temporarily learn Divination or Necromancy spells, and later improve control over their tale results.
mechanical_tags: bonus damage or healing through focus
build_notes: Spirit, storytelling, Bardic Inspiration, Divination, and Necromancy are central to the subclass text.
Many damage, condition, and movement traits are included at lower weights because they appear as individual possible Spirit Tales rather than constant features.
Support is meaningful because several tales grant buffs, temporary hit points, healing, teleportation, or extra checks.

name: College of Swords
summary: College of Swords bards, called blades, combine weapon performance with spellcasting. Their features add medium armor, scimitar proficiency, melee weapon spellcasting focus, Dueling or Two-Weapon Fighting, Blade Flourishes, increased movement, extra attacks, defensive boosts, area weapon damage, forced movement, and reaction movement.
build_notes: The subclass is a melee spellcaster because it explicitly uses melee weapons as spellcasting focuses and gains martial combat features.
Dueling and two weapon fighting are both tagged because they are the explicit Fighting Style choices.
Mobility and forced movement are meaningful because Blade Flourish directly increases speed and Mobile Flourish pushes the target and moves the bard.

name: College of Valor
summary: College of Valor bards are battle-oriented skalds who inspire heroic martial action. Their features grant medium armor, shields, martial weapons, Combat Inspiration for damage or AC, Extra Attack, and Battle Magic that combines spellcasting with a bonus-action weapon attack.
mechanical_tags: Bardic Inspiration added to weapon damage
Bardic Inspiration added to AC as reaction
bonus-action weapon attack after bard spell
build_notes: The subclass is a martial support bard with stronger armor and weapon access than the base class.
Combat Inspiration supports both offensive damage and defensive AC reactions.
Battle Magic supports the melee spellcaster tag, but the subclass remains more support-oriented than purely striker-oriented.

name: College of Whispers
summary: College of Whispers bards use secrecy, fear, psychic damage, stolen shadows, disguise, and manipulation to exploit others. Their features add psychic weapon damage, frighten targets through conversation, steal a dead humanoid's shadow to impersonate them, and charm creatures through terrifying secret knowledge.
mechanical_tags: extra psychic damage on weapon hit
once per round Bardic Inspiration damage
build_notes: Psychic and fear are defining because Psychic Blades and Words of Terror are the earliest and clearest combat/social mechanics.
Disguise and impersonation are central because Mantle of Whispers lets the bard magically adopt a dead humanoid's persona.
The subclass should be tagged as infiltrator and social manipulation rather than broad battlefield controller.

name: Cleric
summary: Clerics are divine spellcasters who act as conduits for the power of their deities. Their core features emphasize Wisdom-based prepared spellcasting, ritual casting, Channel Divinity, turning and destroying undead, divine intervention, healing, support, and domain-based specialization.
build_notes: The base class is primarily a Wisdom-based divine full caster with strong support and healing identity.
Domain choice significantly changes armor, weapons, damage type, and combat role, so the base class is not over-tagged as melee, blaster, tank, or controller.
Channel Divinity and undead interaction are central class mechanics.

name: Arcana Domain
summary: Arcana Domain clerics serve gods of magic, magical knowledge, and arcane power. Their features grant Arcana proficiency, wizard cantrips, abjuration against otherworldly creatures, spell removal through healing, stronger cleric cantrips, and high-level wizard spell access.
mechanical_tags: wizard cantrips counted as cleric cantrips
turn celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend
build_notes: Arcane and spellcasting traits are central because the domain grants wizard cantrips and later wizard spell choices.
Abjuration is central because Arcane Abjuration is the domain's Channel Divinity.
Healing is secondary because Spell Breaker triggers when restoring hit points but does not make healing the domain's primary identity.

name: Death Domain
summary: Death Domain clerics channel death, negative energy, murder, disease, poison, and undeath. Their features emphasize necromancy cantrips, doubled necromancy targeting, necrotic melee damage, resistance-piercing necrotic damage, and improved necromancy spell targeting.
mechanical_tags: extra necrotic damage on melee hit
build_notes: Necromancy and necrotic damage are defining because every major domain feature reinforces them.
Undead is central to the domain's theme and spell list.
Poison and plague are included at lower weights because the text associates the domain with disease and poison, and the spell list includes poison-related effects.

name: Forge Domain
summary: Forge Domain clerics serve artisan gods of metalwork, creation, armor, weapons, and magic items. Their features grant heavy armor, smith's tools, weapon or armor enhancement, metal item creation, fire resistance and immunity, AC bonuses in heavy armor, and fire-based weapon damage.
mechanical_tags: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing resistance in heavy armor
build_notes: Crafting, smith's tools, heavy armor, and fire are defining traits from the domain description and features.
Tank and high armor class are strongly supported by heavy armor proficiency and later armor-based AC bonuses.
Magic item crafting is supported by Blessing of the Forge and the subclass's focus on making and empowering arms and armor.

name: Grave Domain
summary: Grave Domain clerics guard the boundary between life and death, oppose undeath, and ease dying creatures. Their features maximize healing on creatures at 0 hit points, improve Spare the Dying, detect undead, curse a creature to suffer vulnerability, prevent critical hits, and transfer enemy necrotic damage.
mechanical_tags: maximum healing dice on creature at 0 hit points
Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
build_notes: Death prevention, healing, and undead opposition define this subclass more than raw damage.
Curse and debuffing are meaningful because Path to the Grave makes the next hit against the target much more dangerous.
Reaction-based protection is important because Sentinel at Death's Door cancels critical hits.

name: Knowledge Domain
summary: Knowledge Domain clerics serve gods of learning, understanding, secrets, and lore. Their features grant languages, knowledge skill proficiency and doubled proficiency, temporary skill or tool proficiency, thought reading, Suggestion without a spell slot, stronger cantrip damage, and visions of past events.
mechanical_tags: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion proficiency
doubled proficiency bonus for chosen knowledge skills
Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
build_notes: Knowledge, scholar, expertise, and language utility are defining because the subclass grants languages, knowledge skills, doubled proficiency, and temporary proficiencies.
Divination is central because the spell list and Visions of the Past emphasize information gathering.
Mind control is secondary because Read Thoughts can lead into Suggestion, but it is not the whole subclass identity.

name: Life Domain
summary: Life Domain clerics focus on positive energy, vitality, health, and healing. Their features grant heavy armor, stronger healing spells, Channel Divinity healing, self-healing when healing others, radiant weapon damage, and maximum healing dice.
mechanical_tags: healing pool equal to five times cleric level
build_notes: Healing and support are the defining mechanics of the Life Domain.
Heavy armor is explicit but secondary to the healing identity.
Radiant is included because Divine Strike adds radiant damage, but damage is not the primary role.

name: Light Domain
summary: Light Domain clerics wield radiance, sunlight, fire, vigilance, and truth to burn away darkness and lies. Their features grant the Light cantrip, reaction-based defensive flare, radiant area damage that dispels magical darkness, ally protection through Warding Flare, and an aura that weakens enemy saves against fire or radiant spells.
mechanical_tags: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
enemy disadvantage against fire or radiant spell saves
build_notes: Fire, radiant damage, and area damage are central due to the domain spell list, Radiance of the Dawn, and Corona of Light.
Warding is meaningful because Warding Flare and Improved Flare impose disadvantage on attacks.
Darkness is included because the subclass explicitly dispels magical darkness and is framed as burning away darkness.

name: Nature Domain
summary: Nature Domain clerics serve gods of forests, groves, harvests, animals, plants, and natural forces. Their features grant a druid cantrip, nature-related skill proficiency, heavy armor, charm over beasts and plants, elemental resistance reactions, elemental weapon damage, and command over charmed animals or plants.
mechanical_tags: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival proficiency
Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
reaction resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage
Divine Strike cold, fire, or lightning damage
bonus-action command to charmed animals or plants
build_notes: Nature, beast, plant, and primal traits are central to the domain text and mechanics.
Damage resistance is strongly supported by Dampen Elements.
Heavy armor is explicit but secondary to the nature and elemental-protection identity.

name: Order Domain
summary: Order Domain clerics embody law, discipline, hierarchy, and command. Their features grant heavy armor, Intimidation or Persuasion proficiency, reaction attacks for allies targeted by spells, charming and disarming through Channel Divinity, enchantment spell bonuses, and curse-like divine damage tied to weapon strikes.
mechanical_tags: ally reaction weapon attack after targeted spell
force charmed creatures to drop held items
build_notes: Battlefield commander and support are central because Voice of Authority turns allied spell targeting into immediate weapon attacks.
Enchantment, charm, and command themes are strongly supported by domain spells and Order's Demand.
Heavy armor is explicit but not the subclass's core identity.

name: Peace Domain
summary: Peace Domain clerics create magical bonds that strengthen allies, heal through movement, and let bonded creatures protect each other. Their features emphasize support, buffing attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws, healing, teleportation, redirected damage, and damage resistance.
mechanical_tags: d4 to attack roll, ability check, or saving throw
damage resistance when taking ally damage
build_notes: Support, buffing, and protect allies are defining because Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond are the main subclass mechanics.
Teleportation and redirected damage are central at 6th level through Protective Bond.
Healing is important but not the only identity; the subclass is broader ally-bond support.

name: Tempest Domain
summary: Tempest Domain clerics serve gods of storms, sea, sky, lightning, thunder, violence, courage, and divine wrath. Their features grant heavy armor and martial weapons, reaction lightning or thunder retaliation, maximized lightning or thunder damage, lightning-based pushing, thunder weapon damage, and outdoor flight.
build_notes: Lightning, thunder, and storm are defining because every major combat feature reinforces them.
Forced movement is meaningful because Thunderous Strike pushes creatures after lightning damage.
Flight is significant but later-level and conditional on being outdoors and not underground.

name: Trickery Domain
summary: Trickery Domain clerics serve gods of mischief, deception, theft, rebellion, and subterfuge. Their features enhance Stealth, create illusory duplicates, enable spellcasting through duplicates, grant invisibility, add poison weapon damage, and later create multiple duplicates.
build_notes: Stealth, illusion, and infiltrator are defining traits from Blessing of the Trickster, Invoke Duplicity, and Cloak of Shadows.
Poison is meaningful because Divine Strike explicitly adds poison damage.
Teleportation and shapechanging are lower-weight because they appear through domain spells rather than core class features.

name: Twilight Domain
summary: Twilight Domain clerics guard the transition between light and darkness, comforting allies and protecting them from the horrors of night. Their features grant heavy armor and martial weapons, extended darkvision sharing, initiative advantage, a protective twilight sphere, temporary hit points, charm and fear removal, magical flight in dim light or darkness, and protective cover.
mechanical_tags: bonus-action flight in dim light or darkness
build_notes: Support, protect allies, temporary hit points, and aura are defining because Twilight Sanctuary is the central subclass mechanic.
Flight is significant because Steps of Night grants a magical flying speed in dim light or darkness.
Heavy armor and martial weapons are explicit but secondary to the protective twilight identity.

name: War Domain
summary: War Domain clerics serve gods of battle, heroism, destruction, conquest, and martial excellence. Their features grant heavy armor and martial weapons, bonus-action weapon attacks, major attack roll bonuses for themselves and allies, weapon damage, resistance-granting battle magic, and support for warriors in combat.
mechanical_tags: reaction +10 attack roll bonus for ally
resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical weapons
build_notes: Warrior, offensive fighting, and bonus-action attacks are defining because War Priest directly adds weapon attacks.
Support and battlefield commander are meaningful because War God's Blessing grants a major attack roll bonus to an ally.
Damage resistance is included at lower weight because Avatar of Battle arrives at 17th level.

name: Druid
summary: Druids are Wisdom-based nature spellcasters who draw on the divine essence of nature itself. Their core features emphasize prepared spellcasting, ritual casting, Wild Shape, beast transformation, nature skills, herbalism, and later casting while transformed.
build_notes: The base class is primarily a Wisdom-based full caster with prepared spellcasting and ritual casting.
Wild Shape is a defining class mechanic and supports beast, shapechanging, short rest recovery, and later casting while transformed.
Flight and swimming are low-weight because the base Wild Shape limitations delay access to forms with those movement types.

name: Circle of Dreams
summary: Circle of Dreams druids are tied to the Feywild and dreamlike realms. Their features emphasize fey healing, temporary hit points, guarded rests, stealth and perception bonuses, teleportation, dream travel, and limited spell use without spell slots.
mechanical_tags: Stealth and Perception bonus during rest
Dream, Scrying, or Teleportation Circle without spell slot
build_notes: Healing and support are central because Balm of the Summer Court is the subclass's first major feature.
Teleportation is defining at higher levels through Hidden Paths and Walker in Dreams.
Stealth and Perception are meaningful but situational because they apply inside the rest-protection sphere.

name: Circle of the Land
summary: Circle of the Land druids are mystics and sages whose magic is shaped by the terrain where they were initiated. Their features emphasize extra cantrips, spell slot recovery, always-prepared land spells, terrain traversal, plant and poison protections, and defensive influence over beasts and plants.
build_notes: Spellcasting and utility casting are central because Bonus Cantrip, Natural Recovery, and Circle Spells all improve the druid's spell use.
Terrain traversal is central because Land's Stride directly improves movement through difficult terrain and plants.
Elemental and environment traits are included at moderate or low weights because they vary by land choice rather than applying uniformly.

name: Circle of the Moon
summary: Circle of the Moon druids are fierce guardians of the wilds who use Wild Shape for combat. Their features emphasize bonus-action transformation, stronger beast forms, self-healing while transformed, magical beast-form attacks, elemental transformation, and at-will subtle physical alteration.
mechanical_tags: spend spell slots to heal while transformed
build_notes: Wild Shape, shapechanging, and beast are defining because every subclass feature modifies transformation.
Tank and melee are strongly supported by stronger beast forms and self-healing while transformed.
Elemental is significant at 10th level through Elemental Wild Shape.

name: Circle of the Shepherd
summary: Circle of the Shepherd druids commune with spirits of nature, beasts, and fey to protect vulnerable creatures. Their features emphasize communication with beasts and fey, summoned spirit auras, temporary hit points, attack support, healing support, stronger beast and fey summons, and emergency conjured protectors.
mechanical_tags: Hawk Spirit reaction advantage on attack roll
improved summoned beast and fey hit points
build_notes: Summoning, support, spirit, beast, and fey are defining because the subclass repeatedly improves spirits and conjured beasts or fey.
Aura is central because Spirit Totem creates a recurring aura with different support effects.
Death prevention is secondary because Faithful Summons triggers only when the druid is reduced to 0 hit points or incapacitated against their will.

name: Circle of Spores
summary: Circle of Spores druids find beauty in decay and use fungal magic to connect life, death, and undeath. Their features emphasize necrotic spores, temporary hit points, melee necrotic damage, zombie animation, area spores, and immunity to several conditions.
mechanical_tags: Wild Shape use without beast transformation
build_notes: Necrotic, necromancy, death, and temporary hit points are central because Halo of Spores and Symbiotic Entity define the combat pattern.
Undead is meaningful because Fungal Infestation animates a dead beast or humanoid as a zombie.
Condition immunity is strongly supported by Fungal Body.

name: Circle of Stars
summary: Circle of Stars druids draw on starlight, constellations, heavenly patterns, and cosmic omens. Their features emphasize a star map focus, Guidance, Guiding Bolt, starry transformation, radiant ranged attacks, healing, concentration support, divination-like reaction bonuses and penalties, flight, and resistance to weapon damage while in Starry Form.
mechanical_tags: minimum roll for Intelligence checks, Wisdom checks, and concentration saves
build_notes: Cosmic, radiant, divination, and support are central because Star Map, Starry Form, and Cosmic Omen all reinforce those mechanics.
Healing and ranged damage are both meaningful because Chalice and Archer are recurring Starry Form options.
Flight and damage resistance are significant but arrive through later Starry Form improvements.

name: Circle of Wildfire
summary: Circle of Wildfire druids bond with a primal wildfire spirit that embodies both destruction and creation. Their features emphasize fire spells, healing spells, a summoned elemental spirit, fire damage, flight, teleportation, bonus healing or fire damage, reaction-based healing or fire damage from death, and death prevention through the spirit.
mechanical_tags: Wild Shape use without beast transformation
bonus to fire damage or healing roll
spell can originate from wildfire spirit
reaction healing or fire damage from spectral flame
visual_or_flavor_tags: humanoid figure made of burning branches
build_notes: Fire, spirit, companion feature, and summoning are defining because Summon Wildfire Spirit is the subclass's central mechanic.
Healing is also central because the circle spell list and Enhanced Bond explicitly improve restorative magic.
Teleportation is strongly supported by Fiery Teleportation, which can move the spirit and nearby willing creatures.

name: Fighter
summary: Fighters are martial combatants defined by mastery of weapons, armor, fighting styles, stamina, extra actions, repeated attacks, and saving throw resilience. Their core identity supports melee, ranged, defensive, shield, heavy weapon, archery, two-weapon, thrown weapon, unarmed, and tactical combat styles.
mechanical_tags: Extra Attack scaling to four attacks
build_notes: The class is primarily martial and supports both Strength and Dexterity builds.
Extra Attack and Action Surge are defining action-economy mechanics.
Fighting Style allows many combat identities, so individual styles are tagged but not all at maximum weight.

name: Arcane Archer
summary: Arcane Archers weave magic into arrows to produce supernatural ranged effects. Their features emphasize archery, magical shots, Intelligence-based save DCs, cantrip access, magical arrows, rerouting missed shots, and a wide spread of arcane effects such as banishment, charm, force damage, necrotic damage, poison, piercing lines, seeking arrows, and shadowed vision.
build_notes: Ranged and archery are defining because Arcane Shot applies to arrows fired from a shortbow or longbow.
Intelligence is important because Arcane Shot save DC uses Intelligence.
Many magic-school and damage traits are moderate because they are optional Arcane Shot choices rather than always-on subclass mechanics.

name: Banneret
summary: Bannerets are knightly leaders who inspire allies through brave deeds in battle. Their features extend Second Wind healing to allies, improve Persuasion, grant ally reaction attacks through Action Surge, and share Indomitable saving throw rerolls with an ally.
mechanical_tags: ally reaction weapon attack after Action Surge
build_notes: Support, leadership, and battlefield commander are defining because every subclass feature improves allies or social command.
Persuasion is central because Royal Envoy grants Persuasion proficiency and doubled proficiency bonus.
Healing is secondary because Rallying Cry only triggers when using Second Wind.

name: Battle Master
summary: Battle Masters use learned martial techniques powered by superiority dice. Their subclass identity emphasizes maneuvers, tactical combat, Strength or Dexterity-based save DCs, short-rest resource recovery, artisan training, and observation-based assessment of enemies.
mechanical_tags: maneuver save DC using Strength or Dexterity
build_notes: Maneuvers and superiority dice are defining because all primary subclass combat features use them.
The subclass supports many tactical roles depending on maneuver choice, so control, support, offense, and defense are weighted below maneuvers.
Strength and Dexterity are both primary because maneuver save DC can use either.

name: Cavalier
summary: Cavaliers excel at mounted combat, protection, marking enemies, punishing attacks against allies, improving AC and resistance for nearby creatures, locking down movement, knocking foes prone after charges, and making many opportunity attacks. The subclass is a defender built around close-range control and protective reactions.
mechanical_tags: special melee weapon attack against marked target
damage resistance if attack still hits
opportunity attacks against movement within reach
special opportunity attack reaction on every creature's turn
build_notes: Mounted combat is defining from the subclass description and Born to the Saddle.
Defender, protector, and battlefield control are strongly supported by Unwavering Mark, Warding Maneuver, Hold the Line, and Vigilant Defender.
Constitution is important because Warding Maneuver uses Constitution modifier for uses.

name: Champion
summary: Champions focus on raw physical power, athletic excellence, improved critical hits, additional fighting style flexibility, and battlefield resilience. Their features improve critical hit range, enhance physical checks and jumping, add a second Fighting Style, further expand critical range, and provide regeneration while badly wounded.
mechanical_tags: half proficiency to Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution checks
hit point regeneration while below half hit points
build_notes: Critical hits are the defining subclass mechanic through Improved Critical and Superior Critical.
Physical ability scores are all relevant because Remarkable Athlete applies to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution checks.
Regeneration and self-healing are late but mechanically clear through Survivor.

name: Echo Knight
summary: Echo Knights summon magical echoes of unrealized timelines to fight from alternate positions. Their features emphasize echo manifestation, teleportation, remote attacks, opportunity attacks from the echo's space, extra melee attacks, scouting through the echo, ally protection, temporary hit points when echoes are destroyed, and multiple echoes at high level.
mechanical_tags: extra melee attack from echo position
remote sight and hearing through echo
temporary hit points when echo is destroyed
visual_or_flavor_tags: cycling swarm of shadows and strikes
build_notes: Echo magic and teleportation are defining because Manifest Echo and echo swapping are core subclass mechanics.
Constitution is important because Unleash Incarnation and Reclaim Potential use Constitution modifier for uses or scaling.
Scout is meaningful because Echo Avatar allows remote senses up to 1,000 feet.

name: Eldritch Knight
summary: Eldritch Knights combine fighter martial mastery with wizard-style spellcasting. Their features emphasize Intelligence-based known spellcasting, cantrips, abjuration, evocation, weapon bonding and weapon teleportation, cantrip-to-weapon attack action economy, spell-save debuffing after weapon hits, teleportation through Action Surge, and improved bonus-action weapon attacks after spells.
mechanical_tags: disadvantage on next save against spell after weapon hit
build_notes: Melee spellcaster, arcane, and third caster are defining because the subclass explicitly augments fighter martial prowess with wizard spellcasting.
Intelligence is central because it is the spellcasting ability.
Teleportation is meaningful because Weapon Bond teleports a weapon and Arcane Charge teleports the fighter after Action Surge.

name: Psi Warrior
summary: Psi Warriors augment martial combat with psionic energy, telekinetic force, protective barriers, mental discipline, flight, forced movement, and force damage. Their features use Psionic Energy dice to reduce damage, add force damage to weapon hits, move objects or willing creatures, fly briefly, knock or move enemies, resist psychic damage, end charm or fear, grant cover to allies, and enhance weapon strikes with telekinetic energy.
build_notes: Psionics, telekinesis, and force are defining because every core feature uses psionic energy, telekinetic effects, or force damage.
Intelligence is central because several features add Intelligence modifier or use Intelligence-based DCs.
Protect allies and damage reduction are strong because Protective Field and Bulwark of Force are major recurring defensive features.

name: Rune Knight
summary: Rune Knights use giant-derived rune magic to empower equipment and grow in size during battle. Their features emphasize smith's tools, Giant language, magical runes, Constitution-based rune save DCs, giant transformation, extra weapon damage, advantage on physical checks and saves, ally protection, redirected attacks, fire restraints, charm-like control, damage resistance, and runic support.
build_notes: Rune magic and giant traits are defining because the subclass is explicitly built around giant rune craft.
Constitution is central because Rune Magic save DC uses Constitution.
The subclass is broad because different runes provide different utility, control, protection, and damage effects.

name: Samurai
summary: Samurai draw on intense fighting spirit, discipline, social poise, and unbreakable resolve. Their features grant bonus proficiency or language, advantage on weapon attacks with temporary hit points, Persuasion bonuses from Wisdom, additional mental saving throw proficiency, regained Fighting Spirit when initiative is rolled, extra weapon attacks by trading advantage, and a reaction-based extra turn when reduced to 0 hit points.
mechanical_tags: History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion proficiency
trade advantage for additional weapon attack
reaction extra turn at 0 hit points
build_notes: Temporary hit points and offensive fighting are central because Fighting Spirit grants both attack advantage and temporary hit points.
Wisdom is important because Elegant Courtier adds Wisdom modifier to Persuasion and grants Wisdom saving throw proficiency.
Death prevention is significant because Strength Before Death delays unconsciousness and grants an immediate extra turn at 0 hit points.

name: Monk
summary: Monks magically harness ki through martial arts, defensive focus, speed, and disciplined body control. Their core mechanics emphasize Dexterity and Wisdom, unarmed strikes, monk weapons, ki points, bonus-action attacks, mobility, unarmored defense, stunning, evasion, condition removal, poison immunity, universal communication, saving throw mastery, invisibility, and damage resistance.
mechanical_tags: Tongue of the Sun and Moon
build_notes: The class is primarily martial, mobility-focused, unarmored, Dexterity-based, and Wisdom-scaling.
Ki is the defining class resource and recovers on a short or long rest after meditation.
The base class is not tagged as spellcasting because its magical effects are primarily ki features rather than normal spellcasting.

name: Way of Mercy
summary: Way of Mercy monks manipulate life force to heal the wounded and bring swift death to those beyond help. Their features emphasize Medicine, Insight, herbalism, healing touch, necrotic unarmed damage, disease and condition removal, poisoned condition application, and resurrection.
build_notes: Healing is the defining mechanic because Hands of Healing and later features repeatedly improve restorative use.
Necrotic and poison traits are strongly supported by Hands of Harm and Physician's Touch.
Revival is significant at high level through Hand of Ultimate Mercy.

name: Way of the Ascendant Dragon
summary: Way of the Ascendant Dragon monks emulate dragons by channeling draconic ki through unarmed strikes, breath-like area attacks, spectral wings, auras, fear, resistance, and heightened senses. The subclass centers on dragon power, elemental damage choice, flight, intimidation or persuasion presence, and ally protection.
build_notes: Dragon and elemental damage traits are central because Draconic Strike, Breath of the Dragon, Aspect of the Wyrm, and Explosive Fury all use dragon-associated damage choices.
Flight is significant because Wings Unfurled grants a flying speed when using Step of the Wind.
Support is secondary but clear through the resistance aura that benefits allies.

name: Way of the Astral Self
summary: Way of the Astral Self monks manifest spectral arms, visage, body, and awakened self through ki. Their features emphasize Wisdom-based unarmed attacks, force damage, reach, darkness sight, social utility, energy deflection, extra damage, improved armor class, and additional astral-arm attacks.
mechanical_tags: Wisdom for Strength checks and saves
build_notes: Wisdom is defining because the subclass repeatedly substitutes Wisdom for physical attack, damage, and Strength-related rolls.
Force damage and unarmed reach are central to Arms of the Astral Self.
Damage reduction is meaningful because Deflect Energy reduces several elemental and force damage types.

name: Way of the Drunken Master
summary: Way of the Drunken Master monks use erratic, unpredictable movement to frustrate enemies and turn mistakes against them. Their features emphasize Performance, brewer's supplies, mobility after Flurry of Blows, easier recovery from prone, redirected enemy attacks, canceling disadvantage, and many attacks against groups.
mechanical_tags: additional Flurry of Blows attacks against different creatures
build_notes: Mobility and hit-and-run tactics are defining because Drunken Technique grants Disengage and speed after Flurry of Blows.
Redirect damage is meaningful because Tipsy Sway can cause a missed melee attack to hit another nearby creature.
Performance and brewer's supplies are explicit subclass proficiencies.

name: Way of the Four Elements
summary: Way of the Four Elements monks use ki to harness elemental disciplines and bend the forces of creation as extensions of their bodies. The page text emphasizes elemental disciplines, spell-like effects powered by ki, optional spell casting through disciplines, and increasing spell level by spending additional ki.
mechanical_tags: spend additional ki to increase spell level
build_notes: Elemental and ki are defining because the subclass is entirely built around elemental disciplines powered by ki.
Spellcasting is included because some disciplines explicitly allow casting spells using normal spell rules except material components.
Specific damage types are omitted because the provided subclass page text does not directly list individual elemental discipline effects.
review_reasons: The page references a separate elemental discipline list, so the subclass page alone does not fully expose all available discipline mechanics.
Specific elemental damage tags were omitted unless directly supported by the provided subclass page text.

name: Way of the Kensei
summary: Way of the Kensei monks master weapons until the weapon becomes an extension of the body. Their features emphasize selected melee and ranged weapons as monk weapons, defensive parrying, stronger ranged weapon damage, artisan tool proficiency, magical weapon attacks, extra weapon damage, ki-enhanced attack and damage bonuses, and rerolls for missed weapon attacks.
mechanical_tags: +2 AC while holding melee kensei weapon
build_notes: Melee and ranged weapon use are both central because the subclass explicitly chooses one melee and one ranged kensei weapon at 3rd level.
High armor class and defensive fighting are supported by Agile Parry.
Tool traits are included because Way of the Brush grants calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies proficiency.

name: Way of the Long Death
summary: Way of the Long Death monks study dying and use that knowledge to create a deadly martial style. Their features emphasize temporary hit points from nearby kills, frightening nearby creatures, avoiding death at 0 hit points, and spending ki for high necrotic touch damage.
mechanical_tags: temporary hit points after reducing nearby creature to 0 hit points
spend ki to remain at 1 hit point
build_notes: Death, temporary hit points, and death prevention are defining because the subclass repeatedly rewards proximity to death or avoids death.
Necrotic is central because Touch of the Long Death deals necrotic damage.
Fear is meaningful because Hour of Reaping frightens creatures in a 30-foot area.

name: Way of the Open Hand
summary: Way of the Open Hand monks are masters of martial arts combat who manipulate enemy ki, heal themselves, protect themselves through meditation, and deliver lethal vibrations through unarmed strikes. Their features emphasize prone, pushing, reaction denial, self-healing, warding, necrotic damage, and instant reduction to 0 hit points.
build_notes: Battlefield control is central because Open Hand Technique adds prone, push, and reaction denial to Flurry of Blows.
Self-healing is meaningful through Wholeness of Body.
Single-target damage is supported at high level by Quivering Palm.

name: Way of Shadow
summary: Way of Shadow monks value stealth, subterfuge, assassination, and obedience to secretive traditions. Their features use ki to duplicate shadow-related spells, grant Minor Illusion, teleport between shadows, become invisible in dim light or darkness, and make reaction melee attacks when enemies are distracted.
mechanical_tags: cast Pass Without Trace with ki
bonus-action teleport in dim light or darkness
invisibility in dim light or darkness
build_notes: Stealth, shadow, darkness, and teleportation are defining because the subclass's main features revolve around shadow magic and movement through darkness.
Assassin and spy are supported by the page's direct description of these monks as spies and assassins.
Spellcasting is secondary because Shadow Arts duplicates specific spell effects through ki rather than granting normal spellcasting.

name: Way of the Sun Soul
summary: Way of the Sun Soul monks channel life energy into searing magical radiance. Their features emphasize ranged radiant spell attacks, bonus-action radiant attacks, fire spell waves, radiant explosions, bright-light aura, and reaction radiant retaliation.
build_notes: Radiant, light, ranged, and blaster are defining because the subclass's core attack option is a ranged radiant spell attack.
Area damage is meaningful through Searing Arc Strike and Searing Sunburst.
Fire is included because Searing Arc Strike casts Burning Hands.

name: Ranger
summary: Rangers are martial wilderness warriors who combine weapon combat, tracking, exploration, survival, and Wisdom-based spellcasting. Their core identity emphasizes favored enemies or favored foes, terrain expertise, fighting styles, Extra Attack, half-casting, mobility through natural environments, stealth, perception, survival, and later senses and ambush-oriented combat.
build_notes: The class is primarily martial, skill-based, exploration-focused, and half-casting.
Dexterity and Wisdom are the most important base class ability scores because the class supports ranged or finesse combat, exploration skills, and spellcasting.
The base class supports both melee and ranged builds, but ranged combat and scouting are stronger class-level identities.

name: Beast Master Conclave
summary: Beast Master rangers form a close fighting bond with a beast companion. The subclass centers on commanding an animal companion, improving its attacks and defenses, coordinating attacks with it, sharing spells, and fighting alongside a beast as a core combat partner.
build_notes: Companion feature, pet, and beast are defining because the subclass's main mechanic is fighting alongside a beast companion.
Action economy is meaningful because the ranger spends actions or bonus actions to command the companion depending on the feature version.
Spellcasting is secondary because Share Spells modifies spells but does not make spellcasting the primary subclass identity.

name: Drakewarden
summary: Drakewardens magically bond with a draconic spirit that takes physical form as a drake companion. Their features emphasize a dragon companion, elemental damage, protective reactions, language utility, increased drake size, flight, breath-like area damage, and shared resistance.
build_notes: Dragon and companion feature are defining because the subclass revolves around a summoned drake companion.
Elemental damage traits are supported by the drake's draconic essence and breath feature.
Mounted combat and flight become meaningful once the drake grows and gains a flying speed.

name: Fey Wanderer
summary: Fey Wanderers blend ranger magic with fey mystique, charm, fear, psychic damage, social grace, and summoned fey aid. Their features emphasize Charisma-like social benefits from Wisdom, psychic weapon damage, charm and fear resistance or redirection, summoning fey, and teleportation.
build_notes: Fey, charm, fear, and psychic are defining because they recur across Dreadful Strikes, Beguiling Twist, and the spell list.
Face is strongly supported because Otherworldly Glamour adds Wisdom to Charisma checks and grants a social skill.
Teleportation is meaningful through Misty Step and later Misty Wanderer.

name: Gloom Stalker Conclave
summary: Gloom Stalkers are ambushers who hunt threats in darkness and underground places. Their features emphasize stealth, initiative, first-round burst damage, darkness-based invisibility, Wisdom saving throw protection, extra attacks after misses, and defensive attack redirection.
mechanical_tags: extra walking speed on first turn
extra weapon damage on first-turn attack
build_notes: Ambush, initiative bonus, darkness, and stealth are defining because the subclass's early features heavily reinforce first-strike tactics.
Nova damage is meaningful because Dread Ambusher adds an extra first-turn attack with extra damage.
Invisibility is supported specifically against creatures relying on darkvision while the ranger is in darkness.

name: Horizon Walker Conclave
summary: Horizon Walkers guard the world against planar threats and wield planar magic in combat. Their features emphasize portal detection, force damage, teleportation, ethereal travel, extra attacks against multiple enemies, and resistance to damage from attacks.
build_notes: Force damage and teleportation are defining because Planar Warrior and Distant Strike are central combat features.
Damage resistance is meaningful through Spectral Defense.
Divination is secondary because Detect Portal locates planar portals but does not define the entire subclass.

name: Hunter Conclave
summary: Hunters specialize in fighting many kinds of threats through flexible combat options. Their features emphasize extra damage, reaction attacks, multiattack defense, resistance to area effects, defensive escape from larger enemies, attacks against groups, and strong reactions against missed attacks.
build_notes: The subclass is a flexible martial striker with multiple selectable offensive and defensive options.
Ranged and melee are both meaningful because Volley and Whirlwind Attack support different weapon approaches.
The page offers choices at several levels, so weights avoid treating every selectable option as equally defining.

name: Monster Slayer Conclave
summary: Monster Slayers are trained to defeat supernatural threats, spellcasters, vampires, dragons, fey, fiends, and other magical enemies. Their features emphasize identifying enemy defenses, single-target damage, saving throw bonuses, anti-magic interruption, and reaction-based counterattacks against a marked foe.
mechanical_tags: learn damage immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities
extra weapon damage once per turn
saving throw and grapple escape bonus against target
reaction weapon attack against saving throw source
build_notes: Anti-mage and mage hunter are defining because Magic-User's Nemesis directly interferes with spellcasting and teleportation.
Single-target damage is central because Slayer's Prey marks one creature for recurring damage.
Saving throw bonus is strongly supported by Supernatural Defense and Slayer's Counter.

name: Swarmkeeper
summary: Swarmkeepers bond with a nature spirit swarm that assists attacks, moves creatures, moves the ranger, protects the ranger, and eventually disperses or teleports them. The subclass emphasizes forced movement, mobility, piercing damage, control, Mage Hand, flight, defensive resistance, and swarm-flavored utility.
build_notes: Forced movement and battlefield control are defining because Gathered Swarm and Mighty Swarm repeatedly move targets or the ranger.
Piercing damage is supported by Gathered Swarm's extra damage option.
Flight and teleportation are significant but come from later subclass features.

name: Rogue
summary: Rogues rely on skill, stealth, agility, and exploiting vulnerabilities to solve problems and strike precisely. Their core mechanics emphasize Dexterity, Expertise, Sneak Attack with finesse or ranged weapons, thieves' tools, Cunning Action, Steady Aim, Uncanny Dodge, Evasion, Reliable Talent, hidden or invisible creature awareness, Wisdom saving throws, and turning failure into success.
build_notes: The class is primarily skill-based, Dexterity-based, stealth-oriented, and single-target damage focused.
Sneak Attack is the central offensive mechanic and is restricted to finesse or ranged weapons.
Cunning Action, Uncanny Dodge, and Evasion make the class mobile and evasive rather than armor-heavy.

name: Arcane Trickster
summary: Arcane Tricksters blend rogue stealth and agility with wizard magic focused mainly on enchantment and illusion. Their features emphasize Intelligence-based third-caster spellcasting, Mage Hand legerdemain, invisible remote manipulation, magical ambushes from hiding, bonus-action distraction, and stealing spells from other casters.
build_notes: Spellcasting, third caster, Intelligence, enchantment, and illusion are defining because the subclass directly grants wizard spellcasting with a school restriction.
Stealth and ambush remain important because Magical Ambush rewards casting while hidden.
Anti-mage is secondary because Spell Thief is a high-level limited-use feature rather than the primary identity.

name: Assassin
summary: Assassins focus on death, stealth, poison, disguise, false identities, impersonation, and surprise attacks. Their features grant disguise and poison kit proficiency, advantage against creatures that have not acted, automatic critical hits against surprised creatures, durable false identities, mimicry, and doubled damage against surprised targets.
mechanical_tags: advantage against creatures that have not acted
double attack damage against surprised target
build_notes: Ambush, critical hits, and nova damage are defining because Assassinate and Death Strike reward surprise and acting before enemies.
Disguise, impersonation, and poison are central because the subclass explicitly grants tool proficiencies and later false identity and mimicry features.
The subclass should be tagged as infiltrator and assassin more strongly than general sustained damage.

name: Inquisitive
summary: Inquisitives excel at rooting out secrets, unraveling mysteries, detecting lies, reading intent, and exploiting weaknesses. Their features emphasize Insight, Perception, Investigation, bonus-action clue detection, Sneak Attack through tactical analysis, detecting illusions and shapechangers, and increased Sneak Attack damage against studied targets.
mechanical_tags: minimum Insight roll for detecting lies
Sneak Attack without advantage after Insight contest
advantage on Perception or Investigation with limited movement
sense illusions, shapechangers, and sensory deception
build_notes: Insight, Perception, and Investigation are defining because the subclass repeatedly improves these checks.
Sneak Attack is central because Insightful Fighting and Eye for Weakness directly modify how Sneak Attack is enabled and improved.
Divination is low-to-moderate because Unerring Eye detects deception-like magic but does not grant spellcasting.

name: Mastermind
summary: Masterminds focus on influence, secrets, intrigue, tactics, disguise, forgery, languages, mimicry, and manipulating others. Their features emphasize social infiltration, bonus-action Help at range, reading enemy capabilities, redirecting attacks, protecting their thoughts from telepathy, and defeating magical truth detection.
mechanical_tags: learn relative mental ability scores or class levels
build_notes: Social manipulation, disguise, impersonation, and language utility are defining because Master of Intrigue anchors the subclass identity.
Support and battlefield commander are strongly supported by Master of Tactics, which improves the Help action.
Redirect damage is meaningful because Misdirection can transfer an attack meant for the rogue to another creature.

name: Phantom
summary: Phantoms are rogues with a mystical connection to death who draw knowledge and power from the dead. Their features emphasize temporary skill or tool proficiency, necrotic damage through Sneak Attack, soul trinkets, death and Constitution saving throw support, spirit questioning, ghost-like flight and phasing, and deeper association with death.
mechanical_tags: secondary necrotic damage after Sneak Attack
advantage on death and Constitution saving throws
build_notes: Death, ghost, spirit, and necrotic are defining because the subclass repeatedly invokes dead souls and necrotic damage.
Skill flexibility is meaningful because Whispers of the Dead grants a temporary skill or tool proficiency after rests.
Flight is significant but comes from the 13th-level Ghost Walk feature.

name: Scout
summary: Scouts are wilderness rogues who excel at stealth, survival, scouting, ambushes, mobility, and striking quickly. Their features emphasize reaction movement without opportunity attacks, Nature and Survival expertise, increased speed, initiative advantage, ally attack advantage against an ambushed target, and bonus-action attacks with additional Sneak Attack potential.
mechanical_tags: doubled proficiency for Nature and Survival
climbing and swimming speed increase if present
second Sneak Attack against different target
visual_or_flavor_tags: eyes and ears of war bands
build_notes: Scout, survivalist, stealth, and mobility are defining because every subclass feature supports movement, scouting, or wilderness skill.
Ambush is strongly supported by Ambush Master and the subclass description.
Support is secondary because Ambush Master helps allies attack one target during the first round.

name: Soulknife
summary: Soulknives use psionic power to infiltrate, communicate silently, improve failed skill or tool checks, and manifest psychic blades. Their features emphasize psionic resource dice, telepathy, psychic finesse thrown weapons, bonus-action psychic blade attacks, teleportation, invisibility, and stunning a creature through its mind.
build_notes: Psionics, psychic, and thrown weapons are defining because Psychic Blades and Psionic Energy dice drive the subclass.
Telepathy and infiltration are central because Psychic Whispers is explicitly described as ideal for quiet infiltration.
Teleportation, invisibility, and stunning are significant later features tied to psionic resource use.

name: Swashbuckler
summary: Swashbucklers are blade-focused rogues who rely on speed, elegance, charm, and performance-like melee combat. Their features emphasize melee hit-and-run tactics, initiative bonuses from Charisma, one-on-one Sneak Attack, social charm or taunting through Persuasion, Acrobatics or Athletics advantage, and rerolling missed attacks.
mechanical_tags: melee attack prevents opportunity attacks from target
hostile creature attack disadvantage against others
bonus-action advantage on Acrobatics or Athletics
build_notes: Duelist, melee, and hit-and-run are defining because Fancy Footwork and Rakish Audacity support mobile one-on-one melee combat.
Charisma and social manipulation are important because initiative and Panache both depend on charm and social presence.
Two weapon fighting is included at moderate weight because the page explicitly says the subclass can fight with two weapons.

name: Thief
summary: Thieves hone larcenous skills for burglary, treasure seeking, exploration, delving, investigation, and using magic items outside normal limits. Their features emphasize bonus-action Sleight of Hand, thieves' tools, traps, locks, object interaction, climbing, jumping, stealth, magic item use, ambushes, and taking two turns in the first round of combat.
mechanical_tags: bonus-action thieves' tools for traps and locks
climbing no longer costs extra movement
advantage on Stealth with limited movement
ignore class, race, and level magic item requirements
two turns in first combat round
build_notes: Sleight of Hand, thieves' tools, traps, locks, and bonus action are defining because Fast Hands is the core early feature.
Climbing and mobility are meaningful through Second-Story Work.
Magic item use is important at higher levels, but the allowed trait list does not include a direct 'magic item use' trait, so it is represented through utility and mechanical tags.

name: Sorcerer
summary: Sorcerers are Charisma-based full spellcasters whose magic comes from innate power rather than study or divine preparation. Their core mechanics emphasize known spells, cantrips, sorcery points, Flexible Casting, Metamagic, Constitution saving throws, and late-game sorcery point recovery.
build_notes: The class is primarily a Charisma-based full caster built around known spells, sorcery points, and Metamagic.
Constitution is important because the class has Constitution saving throw proficiency and often needs to maintain concentration.
The base class supports blasting, control, buffing, and utility through spell choice, but Metamagic and sorcery points are the defining class identity.

name: Aberrant Mind
summary: Aberrant Mind sorcerers are touched by alien, Far Realm, or mind-warping influence. Their features emphasize psionic spells, telepathic communication, sorcery-point spellcasting without normal components, psychic resistance, charm and fear protection, body transformation, flight, swimming, invisibility detection, teleportation, forced movement, and force damage.
mechanical_tags: cast psionic spells with sorcery points
build_notes: Psionics, telepathy, and aberration are defining because the subclass grants psionic spells and telepathic communication immediately.
Psychic is central through the subclass theme and Psychic Defenses.
Flight, swimming, and invisibility detection are meaningful but tied to Revelation in Flesh options rather than constant passive features.

name: Clockwork Soul
summary: Clockwork Soul sorcerers are tied to cosmic order and the plane of perfect law. Their features emphasize restoring balance, expanded abjuration and transmutation spells, canceling advantage or disadvantage, protective wards, damage reduction, stabilizing rolls, and repairing or ending harmful effects.
mechanical_tags: attack rolls against sorcerer cannot benefit from advantage
build_notes: Clockwork and order are defining because the subclass is explicitly built around law, balance, and mechanical order.
Support, warding, and damage reduction are central through Restore Balance and Bastion of Law.
Abjuration is strongly supported by Clockwork Magic and the protective feature set.

name: Draconic Bloodline
summary: Draconic Bloodline sorcerers trace their innate magic to dragon ancestry. Their features emphasize draconic resilience, improved armor class, extra hit points, elemental damage affinity, elemental resistance, wings and flight, and a fear or charm aura.
mechanical_tags: base AC while not wearing armor
Charisma modifier to matching elemental spell damage
build_notes: Dragon is defining because the subclass requires choosing a dragon ancestor and all later features build on draconic heritage.
High armor class and durability are central through Draconic Resilience.
Elemental traits are included because the ancestry table links the subclass to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage.

name: Divine Soul
summary: Divine Soul sorcerers have innate magic touched by divine power. Their features emphasize access to cleric spells, divine affinity, saving throw or attack roll bonuses, improved healing, spectral wings and flight, and recovery after severe injury.
mechanical_tags: bonus to failed saving throw or missed attack roll
bonus-action self-healing below half hit points
build_notes: Divine and spellcasting are defining because Divine Magic expands the sorcerer spell list to include cleric spells.
Healing and support are strongly supported by cleric spell access and Empowered Healing.
Flight is significant through Otherworldly Wings but arrives at later levels.

name: Lunar Sorcery
summary: Lunar Sorcery sorcerers draw magic from the moon and its changing phases. Their features emphasize phase-based spell access, radiant moonfire, reduced sorcery point costs for certain schools, phase changing, improved Metamagic economy, mobility, invisibility, damage resistance, and area effects tied to lunar power.
mechanical_tags: change lunar phase after long rest
Full Moon awareness and saving throw support
build_notes: Cosmic, spellcasting, sorcery points, and Metamagic are defining because the subclass revolves around lunar phases and sorcery point economy.
Radiant and light are supported by Moon Fire and moon-themed features.
Several spell school traits are included because Lunar Boons explicitly associates phases with schools of magic.

name: Shadow Magic
summary: Shadow Magic sorcerers are touched by the Shadowfell and wield gloom, darkness, and deathly resilience. Their features emphasize darkvision, magical darkness, death prevention, summoning a shadow hound, debuffing a target's saving throws, teleportation through dim light or darkness, and transforming into a resistant shadow form.
mechanical_tags: Charisma save to avoid dropping to 0 hit points
target has disadvantage on saving throws against sorcerer spells
bonus-action teleportation in dim light or darkness
damage resistance except force and radiant
build_notes: Shadow and darkness are defining because the subclass begins with darkvision and magical darkness and later teleports through dim light or darkness.
Death prevention is central through Strength of the Grave.
Summoning and companion feature are meaningful because Hound of Ill Omen creates a hostile-focused shadow hound that affects enemy saves.

name: Storm Sorcery
summary: Storm Sorcery sorcerers command wind, rain, lightning, and thunder. Their features emphasize short bursts of flight after spellcasting, storm language, lightning and thunder resistance, area lightning or thunder damage after spellcasting, weather control, ally-granted flight, and retaliation against melee attackers.
mechanical_tags: area lightning or thunder damage after spellcasting
build_notes: Storm, lightning, thunder, and flight are defining because nearly every subclass feature uses those elements or movement through storm magic.
Area damage is meaningful through Heart of the Storm.
Support is secondary because Wind Soul can grant flight to allies, but the subclass is mostly mobility and elemental damage focused.

name: Wild Magic
summary: Wild Magic sorcerers channel chaotic innate magic that can surge unpredictably. Their features emphasize random magical surges, advantage generation, bendable attack rolls, ability checks, or saving throws, controlled luck manipulation, damage bonuses, and later limited control over surge outcomes.
mechanical_tags: advantage on attack roll, ability check, or saving throw
reaction bonus or penalty to another creature's roll
build_notes: Spellcasting, sorcery points, and roll manipulation are defining because the subclass revolves around Wild Magic Surge, Tides of Chaos, and Bend Luck.
Buffing and debuffing are supported by Tides of Chaos and Bend Luck changing roll outcomes.
Specific movement, damage, shapechanging, and summoning traits are low-weight because they appear as possible surge outcomes rather than stable subclass identity.

name: Warlock
summary: Warlocks are Charisma-based pact spellcasters who gain magic through bargains with otherworldly patrons. Their core identity emphasizes Pact Magic, short-rest spell slot recovery, Eldritch Invocations, Pact Boons, cantrips, known spells, and customizable occult power.
build_notes: The class is primarily a Charisma-based pact caster with short-rest spell slot recovery.
Eldritch Invocations and Pact Boons are defining because they customize the warlock's core mechanics.
The base class should not be over-tagged with patron-specific themes such as fiend, fey, celestial, sea, or undead.

name: Archfey
summary: Archfey warlocks serve powerful fey patrons and gain magic of charm, fear, illusion, escape, and misty disappearance. Their features emphasize frightening or charming nearby creatures, defensive teleportation, immunity to charm with charm reflection, and plunging a creature into an illusory realm.
build_notes: Fey, charm, fear, enchantment, and illusion are defining because the patron features repeatedly use those effects.
Teleportation and invisibility are meaningful through Misty Escape.
Controller and debuffing are supported by Fey Presence and Dark Delirium, but the subclass is more charm/fear focused than general battlefield control.

name: Celestial
summary: Celestial warlocks form pacts with beings from the Upper Planes and gain restorative and radiant power. Their features emphasize healing dice, radiant and fire damage, temporary hit points after rests, resistance to radiant damage, and returning from near death in a burst of radiant energy.
build_notes: Healing is defining because Healing Light is the subclass's first major feature and provides a dedicated healing dice pool.
Radiant and fire are strongly supported by Radiant Soul and the subclass spell list.
Death prevention is meaningful because Searing Vengeance allows the warlock to rise from 0 hit points.

name: Fathomless
summary: Fathomless warlocks serve deep oceanic entities and wield tentacles, cold, lightning, water, and abyssal power. Their features emphasize a spectral tentacle attack, cold damage, movement control, swimming, underwater breathing, damage reduction, cold resistance, summoning a protective tentacle, and teleportation through watery magic.
mechanical_tags: temporary hit points while casting tentacles
build_notes: Sea, cold, swimming, and the spectral tentacle are defining parts of the subclass identity.
Controller is meaningful because the tentacle reduces speed and Grasping Tentacles restrains through the spell effect.
Damage reduction and protect allies are strongly supported by Guardian Coil.

name: Fiend
summary: Fiend warlocks serve lower-planar patrons and gain destructive, resilient, and hellish powers. Their features emphasize temporary hit points from kills, luck-like roll improvement, selectable damage resistance, and hurling a creature through a nightmare realm for psychic damage.
mechanical_tags: temporary hit points after reducing hostile creature to 0 hit points
add d10 to ability check or saving throw
target disappears until end of next turn
build_notes: Fiend and fiendish are defining because the subclass explicitly represents lower-planar patrons.
Temporary hit points are central through Dark One's Blessing.
Damage resistance and saving throw support are meaningful defensive features, while psychic damage is specifically supported by Hurl Through Hell.

name: The Genie
summary: Genie warlocks serve noble genies and receive a magical vessel, elemental damage, sanctuary inside the vessel, flight, damage resistance, and reality-bending wish-like magic. The subclass changes damage and spell themes based on Dao, Djinni, Efreeti, or Marid patron type.
mechanical_tags: damage resistance based on patron kind
build_notes: Elemental is defining because the subclass chooses a genie kind tied to elemental damage and spells.
Flight and damage resistance are significant through Elemental Gift.
The allowed trait list does not include a valid 'wish' trait; Limited Wish is represented in mechanical_tags instead.
review_reasons: The subclass has a major Limited Wish feature, but the allowed trait list has no valid wish or reality-alteration trait.
The source text branches by genie kind, so elemental damage weights represent multiple patron options rather than one fixed build identity.

name: Great Old One
summary: Great Old One warlocks serve inscrutable alien entities and gain powers over thought, madness, telepathy, and mental domination. Their features emphasize one-way telepathy, protective mental interference, psychic resistance, reflected psychic damage, mind control, charm, and creating a charmed thrall.
mechanical_tags: advantage on next attack after miss
thoughts cannot be read by telepathy
build_notes: Eldritch, telepathy, psychic, and mind control are defining because the subclass focuses on alien mental influence.
Damage resistance and retaliation damage are supported by Thought Shield.
Charm is important through Create Thrall, though the subclass is broader than simple social manipulation.

name: Hexblade
summary: Hexblade warlocks form a pact with a mysterious sentient weapon or shadowy force and become weapon-focused pact casters. Their features emphasize Charisma-based weapon attacks, medium armor, shields, curses, critical hits, bonus damage, healing after a cursed target dies, summoning a specter, defensive miss chance, and curse transfer.
mechanical_tags: critical hit on 19 or 20 against cursed target
Charisma for weapon attack and damage
reaction miss chance against cursed target
build_notes: Melee spellcaster, curse, and Charisma are defining because Hex Warrior allows weapon attacks to use Charisma and Hexblade's Curse is the central combat feature.
Medium armor and shield are explicit and important to the subclass's front-line viability.
Summoning and undead are secondary but supported by Accursed Specter.

name: Undead
summary: Undead warlocks draw power from deathless patrons and temporarily assume a terrifying undead form. Their features emphasize fear, temporary hit points, condition immunity, necrotic damage conversion, extra damage, not needing to eat, drink, or breathe, self-revival, spirit projection, flight, resistance, and necromantic damage.
mechanical_tags: no need to eat, drink, or breathe
drop to 1 hit point instead of 0
resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage
necromancy or conjuration spell without components
build_notes: Undead, fear, and necrotic are defining because Form of Dread and Grave Touched are central subclass features.
Death prevention and revival are supported by Necrotic Husk.
Flight and spirit traits become significant through Spirit Projection.

name: Undying
summary: Undying warlocks learn secrets of cheating death from deathless patrons.
